newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures end lower in thin volume.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures end lower in thin volume.

text.p: IPE Brent futures closed slightly higher after slipping in the last hour of trade but brokers said volume was thin and crude was not likely to plunge with gas oil at five year highs.
November Brent closed at $23.11 a barrel, up four cents. It took a dive in the last hour of business but found support at $22.94 a barrel and bounced back.
"There is not much volume. It's very thin and the more active trading was considerably higher. This encourages us into the view that it is cheap rather than weak at the moment," a broker said.
"What we saw was light liquidation and there is a band of support between $22.90-$23. It has a long way to go before it looks nasty," the broker added.
Brent was propelled to an intra-day high of $23.45 a barrel earlier in the day by strong gas oil, which rose to its highest prompt price level since February 1991.
IPE Nov gas oil settled up $7.50 a tonne at $243 a tonne.
Traders said the next target for gas oil was $246 a tonne.
"This would require heating oil to get a boost above 73 cents and so far it looks a bit anaemic," another broker said.
Distillates were boosted by Tuesday's API data which showed U.S. weekly distillate stocks fell to 112.3 million barrels, down 18.7 million from a year ago.
"Crudes have been reticent all day to follow the market and gasoline has been neutral. It is still the gas and heat show," the broker said.
